column4: Visit note | 2025-01-01 03:30 PM | Dr. Zahid Hasan, Gastroenterology | Patient: Farzana Begum, 36, female. Ms. Begum comes in reporting that her stools switch between loose and hard alongside uncomfortable bloating. She is a rickshaw puller and mentions these issues flare on long commutes through traffic in Mirpur. There are no other significant medical conditions noted. On examination: pain score 5/10, BP 131/82 mmHg, pulse 73 bpm, weight 65 kg. Abdomen is soft with mild tenderness in the left lower quadrant. Assessment: Irritable bowel syndrome. Plan: lifestyle and self-care advice only, no new medicine was prescribed at this stage. She was advised to eat regular meals, keep a food diary, and reduce tea, fizzy drinks, and beans. Follow-up in 6 weeks with the food diary.

Visit note | 2025-01-05 03:30 PM | Dr. Imran Kabir, Gastroenterology | Patient: Iffat Khan, 63, female. Mrs. Khan describes a burning sensation behind her breastbone after meals that becomes worse when lying down, along with a sour taste in her mouth. She is a retired civil servant and notes her symptoms are worse after weeks of fried snacks at tea stalls in Rajshahi. She has Type 2 diabetes mellitus. On examination: BMI 30.3, BP 119/73 mmHg, pulse 69 bpm, weight 84 kg. Heart and lung sounds are clear. Assessment: Gastro-oesophageal reflux disease. Plan: lifestyle and self-care advice only, no new medicine was prescribed at this stage. She was advised to eat smaller meals, avoid oily and spicy food late at night, and raise the head of the bed. Follow-up in 1 month.

Visit note | 2025-01-07 03:00 PM | Dr. Imran Kabir, Gastroenterology | Patient: Nurul Faruque, 30, male. Mr. Faruque presents with persistent bloating that gets worse with stress, accompanied by stools that switch between loose and hard. He works as an architect and explains that his symptoms flare on long commutes through traffic in Bashundhara. There are no other notable comorbidities. On examination: pain score 4/10, BP 115/83 mmHg, pulse 85 bpm, weight 97 kg. Abdominal examination is unremarkable except for mild generalized tenderness. Assessment: Irritable bowel syndrome. Follow-up in 6 weeks with the food diary.

Visit note | 2025-01-07 04:00 PM | Dr. Rezaul Karim, Neurology | Patient: Fahim Bepari, 74, male. Mr. Bepari reports tingling like pins and needles and numbness in his toes, which feel worse at night. He works as a homemaker and states these troubles became worse since walking barefoot at home in Khulna. There are no other chronic conditions reported. On examination: reduced sensation at 3 of 10 monofilament test sites, BP 126/79 mmHg, pulse 69 bpm, weight 77 kg. Cranial nerves are intact. Assessment: Peripheral neuropathy. Plan: tests ordered before starting treatment including HbA1c, vitamin B12, and a nerve conduction study; no new medicine was prescribed today. He was advised to check his feet daily for cuts, wear soft closed shoes, and keep his blood sugar under control. Follow-up after the test results are ready.

Visit note | 2025-01-09 04:30 PM | Dr. Imran Kabir, Gastroenterology | Patient: Parvez Rahman, 48, male. Mr. Rahman complains of a burning sensation behind his breastbone after meals and a recurring sour taste in his mouth. He is a fisherman and notes his discomfort is worse after weeks of consuming fried snacks at tea stalls in Savar. He has no other known medical conditions. On examination: BMI 30.8, BP 122/82 mmHg, pulse 88 bpm, weight 48 kg. Abdominal examination reveals mild epigastric tenderness. Assessment: Gastro-oesophageal reflux disease. Plan: referral to General Medicine in this clinic for further assessment; no new medicine was prescribed. He was advised to eat smaller meals, avoid oily and spicy food late at night, and raise the head of the bed. Follow-up after the General Medicine review.

Visit note | 2025-01-11 10:30 AM | Dr. Ishrat Jahan, Psychiatry | Patient: Ziaur Siddique, 71, male. Mr. Siddique states he wakes up tired, worries constantly about his sleep, and has trouble falling asleep most nights, specifically waking at 3 AM every night and being unable to sleep again. He works as a farmer and explains his sleep issues began after a newborn arrived in the family in Rampura. He has Type 2 diabetes mellitus. On examination: Insomnia Severity Index score 23, BP 134/85 mmHg, pulse 76 bpm, weight 77 kg. He appears fatigued but alert. Assessment: Chronic insomnia. Plan: lifestyle and self-care advice only, no new medicine was prescribed at this stage. He was advised to keep fixed sleep and wake times, avoid screens for an hour before bed, and avoid tea after 4 PM. Follow-up in 4 weeks with a sleep diary.

Visit note | 2025-01-11 12:30 PM | Dr. Mostafizur Rahman, Orthopedics | Patient: Shamima Hossain, 64, female. Mrs. Hossain reports experiencing knee pain when using the stairs, a creaking sensation in her knee, and morning stiffness that lasts for a few minutes. She is a homemaker and notes the discomfort is worse after a long sightseeing trip on foot in Savar. She has Bronchial asthma. On examination: BMI 29.5, BP 118/75 mmHg, pulse 86 bpm, weight 91 kg. Right knee shows mild crepitus with no significant effusion. Assessment: Knee osteoarthritis. Plan: referral to Neurology in this clinic for further assessment; no new medicine was prescribed. She was advised to do thigh-strengthening exercises daily, lose weight, and avoid squatting and sitting cross-legged on the floor. Follow-up after the Neurology review.

Visit note | 2025-01-12 02:00 PM | Dr. Sabrina Chowdhury, Cardiology | Patient: Tamim Islam, 75, male. Mr. Islam was found to have high cholesterol on a routine test and mentions a family history of a father who had a heart attack at 55, while currently having no symptoms. He works as a madrasa teacher and the finding was discovered on a pre-employment test in Badda. He has Hypothyroidism. On examination: LDL cholesterol 4.8 mmol/L, BP 113/84 mmHg, pulse 92 bpm, weight 59 kg. Cardiovascular exam is unremarkable. Assessment: Dyslipidaemia. Plan: tests ordered before starting treatment including a fasting lipid profile and liver function tests; no new medicine was prescribed today. He was advised to reduce fried food, red meat, and ghee, walk 30 minutes daily, and aim to lose 3 kg. Follow-up after the test results are ready.

Visit note | 2025-01-12 02:00 PM | Dr. Sharmin Akter, Obstetrics and Gynecology | Patient: Ayesha Haque, 32, female. Ms. Haque visits for irregular periods and extra hair growth on her face. She works as a beautician and noticed weight gain after starting a desk job in Rajshahi. She has Hypothyroidism. On examination: BMI 28.0, BP 118/76 mmHg, pulse 77 bpm, weight 50 kg. Mild hirsutism noted on the jawline. Assessment: Polycystic ovary syndrome. Plan: referral to Endocrinology in this clinic for further assessment; no new medicine was prescribed. She was advised to aim for 5% weight loss, exercise 150 minutes a week, and reduce sugary drinks. Follow-up after the Endocrinology review.

Visit note | 2025-01-12 02:00 PM | Dr. Faisal Karim, Psychiatry | Patient: Shakil Chowdhury, 71, male. Mr. Chowdhury expresses worry about his sleep quality and waking up tired in the mornings. He is a homemaker and shares that his difficulties began after a newborn arrived in the family in Wari. He has Type 2 diabetes mellitus. On examination: Insomnia Severity Index score 15, BP 133/79 mmHg, pulse 83 bpm, weight 75 kg. Mood is anxious but coherent. Assessment: Chronic insomnia. Plan: lifestyle and self-care advice only, no new medicine was prescribed at this stage. He was advised to keep fixed sleep and wake times, avoid screens for an hour before bed, and avoid tea after 4 PM. Follow-up in 4 weeks with a sleep diary.

Visit note | 2025-01-12 03:30 PM | Dr. Anisur Rahman, Ophthalmology | Patient: Mahmuda Awal, 30, female. Mrs. Awal complains of gritty, burning eyes that feel much worse when exposed to air conditioning. She works as a security guard and states her symptoms began after long gaming sessions at home in Banani. She has no other chronic illnesses. On examination: tear break-up time 5 seconds, BP 123/77 mmHg, pulse 79 bpm, weight 48 kg. Conjunctiva is clear with mild dryness signs. Assessment: Dry eye syndrome. Plan: referral to Neurology in this clinic for further assessment; no new medicine was prescribed. She was advised to look away from the screen every 20 minutes, blink often, and use a humidifier. Follow-up after the Neurology review.

Visit note | 2025-01-12 04:30 PM | Dr. Faisal Karim, Psychiatry | Patient: Fahim Matubbar, 22, male. Mr. Matubbar reports poor sleep, constant worry persisting for months, and noticeable muscle tension. He works as a beautician and notes his anxiety is worse since facing job insecurity at a company in Lalbagh. He has no comorbid conditions. On examination: GAD-7 score 16, BP 132/73 mmHg, pulse 73 bpm, weight 66 kg. He is visibly restless. Assessment: Generalized anxiety disorder. Plan: tests ordered before starting treatment including thyroid function tests; no new medicine was prescribed today. He was advised to practise slow breathing daily, reduce tea and coffee, and start counselling sessions. Follow-up after the test results are ready.

Visit note | 2025-01-13 10:00 AM | Dr. Farhana Kabir, General Medicine | Patient: Lipi Siddique, 57, female. Mrs. Siddique presents with brittle nails, a pale appearance, and a feeling of constant tiredness. She works as an electrician and mentions her symptoms started after a stomach illness during a stay in Jatrabari. She has no other medical problems. On examination: haemoglobin 9.4 g/dL, BP 116/85 mmHg, pulse 79 bpm, weight 85 kg. Conjunctivae are pale. Assessment: Iron deficiency anaemia. Plan: lifestyle and self-care advice only, no new medicine was prescribed at this stage. She was advised to eat more lentils, spinach, liver, and eggs, and avoid tea within an hour of meals. Follow-up in 6 weeks with a repeat haemoglobin.

Visit note | 2025-01-14 02:00 PM | Dr. Asif Mahmud, Dermatology | Patient: Ratan Kundu, 22, male. Mr. Kundu complains of spots on his back along with pimples and blackheads on his face. He works as a hotel receptionist and notes his skin condition is worse since working in a hot kitchen in Narayanganj. He denies any systemic illness. On examination: about 25 inflamed spots on the face, BP 131/83 mmHg, pulse 74 bpm, weight 47 kg. Skin shows papules and comedones. Assessment: Acne vulgaris. Plan: lifestyle and self-care advice only, no new medicine was prescribed at this stage. He was advised to wash the face twice daily with a gentle cleanser and not to squeeze spots. Follow-up in 2 months.

Visit note | 2025-01-15 12:00 PM | Dr. Nasrin Sultana, Gastroenterology | Patient: Parvez Rahman, 48, male. Follow-up in 6 weeks with the food diary.

Visit note | 2025-01-18 04:00 PM | Dr. Moinul Haque, Neurology | Patient: Nazmul Faruque, 35, male. Mr. Faruque describes suffering from a throbbing headache on one side of his head accompanied by nausea. He works as a fisherman and notes his episodes are worse since dealing with bright screens at a new job in Chattogram. He has Essential hypertension. On examination: about 10 headache days a month, BP 148/96 mmHg, pulse 73 bpm, weight 45 kg. Neurological examination is otherwise normal. Assessment: Migraine. Plan: tests ordered before starting treatment: no tests; no new medicine was prescribed today. He was advised to keep a headache diary, sleep and eat at regular times, and limit screen time. Follow-up after the test results are ready.
